column1: # hal_rules.tsv - the HAL rule list under D-40 (zero unjustified waivers), 2026-11-20.
# HAL runs with every rule on (flow/2_static/hal_all.f); this list decides which findings the
# gate (tools/hal_zero.py) counts. A rule is OFF only if it judges style or structure, or only
# reports information, never if it can mean a wrong circuit. Every OFF row names the check that
#   RULE  OWN  VENDOR  KIND  REASON  COVERED_BY
#   OWN     on|off   for GARUDA's own RTL
#   VENDOR  on|off   for rtl/third_party (D-40: style waived per IP; correctness reviewed per line)
# A rule not listed is ON in both scopes. An OFF row whose rule fires nowhere fails the gate
# (stale). Findings of ON rules are fixed, or excepted per line in hal_exceptions.tsv.
# ---- information only: HAL reports a fact, not a defect -----------------------------------------

column5: Notes every flop with an asynchronous reset. Asynchronous assert, synchronous release is the chip's reset style (D-14, D-36).
column6: JasperGold RDC (flow/2_static/cdc), reset_ctrl formal, RST* rules stay on

column5: Reports a module's port count.
Reports the number of flops.
Reports that an FSM was recognised.
Reports a signal inferred as a clock.

Reports that a large array is black-boxed for analysis.
Reports an `include directive.
Reports a macro defined twice with the same text.
column6: compile (a differing redefinition is an error)

column1: # ---- structure: timing and hierarchy, judged after synthesis ------------------------------------

column5: A combinational path crosses module boundaries. Every bus decoder, mux and the pipeline's forwarding and hazard logic do this by design; registering them adds a cycle each.
column6: STA after synthesis (trial Genus now, signoff STA at G7); simulation and formal for function

column5: An output is combinational. Same paths as CBPAHI, seen from the driving module.
An input reaches an output through logic only (bus read-data muxes, pass-through of the instruction port).
A chip output is not straight from a flop (pad enables and the JTAG TDO).
column6: I/O constraints in the SDC; chip pad SVA (chip_pads_sva)

column5: A port has a large fanout (the gated clock).
A compare or add is wider than 8 bits (area and timing advice).
A reduction over a wide vector (zero tests and the CSR write-data test written as |x / ~|x for LRGOPR). Area and timing advice.
A module holds both synchronous and asynchronous-reset logic.
Two wires have the same driver (RISC-V immediate fields share instruction bits by the ISA).
An FSM transition flips more than one state bit. Matters only for a state read asynchronously; all GARUDA FSMs are read in their own clock domain.
column6: CDC run (no FSM state crosses a domain)

column5: Several if/case statements in one always block.
A shift by a variable amount (barrel shifter, by design).
Glue logic in the chip top (pad-ring enables).
The tri-state top also holds other logic (pad ring).
A constant in a port connection (parameterised tie-offs).
An expression in a port connection.
A one-bit bus.

column1: # ---- vendored IP only: unused parts of an IP GARUDA does not use --------------------------------
# TO DECIDE (Karthik): these are correctness rules, and D-40 reviews vendor correctness findings
# one by one. Proposed per IP because every finding of the four is the same case: a part of the
# IP that GARUDA's configuration never uses (e.g. INFNOT: 469 FIFO entries past the used depth).
# The alternative is one hal_exceptions.tsv row per line (about 100 lines).

column5: Vendored: ports of the IP that GARUDA's configuration does not use.
column6: the GARUDA wrapper ties or leaves them by intent; the wrapper's own USEPRT stays on

column5: Vendored: registers the IP assigns and GARUDA's configuration never reads.
Vendored: outputs the IP ties to a constant.
Vendored: flops with no fanout in GARUDA's configuration (FIFO entries past the used depth, unused modes); synthesis removes them.
column6: trial synthesis; block regression of the IP
